name: UBS

roles.title: Quantitative Analyst: Rates (Front Office QA)
roles.notes: Live official posting (344368BR, New York, Investment Bank): the Rates QA team builds models 'for the valuation and risk management of the firm's trading positions in interest rate, credit and hybrid derivatives'; requirements name a Masters/PhD-level quantitative background, C++ or Python, derivative pricing and IR-derivatives modelling experience.

roles.title: Electronic Trading Quantitative Analyst
roles.notes: Live official posting (335332BR, New York, Quantitative Analysis & Development team): improves agency algo trading and smart order routing; names microstructure research, TCA, low-latency strategy design, L2/L3 market data, KDB/OneTick plus SQL, Java and Python.

roles.title: Software Engineer (Group Technology)
roles.notes: Role title inferred: UBS's official technology careers page describes an engineering-excellence culture ('UBS has more engineers and developers than many technology companies') with DevOps, cloud and AI tooling emphasis; no specific posting text was quoted for this family.

publishedExpectations.claim: Official Quantitative Analyst. Rates posting: 'Strong academic background in a quantitative field (mathematics, physics, engineering, etc) at a Masters or PhD level'; 'Proficiency in programming (especially C++ or Python)'; 'Knowledge of quantitative finance, derivative pricing and/or machine learning techniques'; plus 'Experience with calibration and risk-based P&L analysis of Interest Rate Option & Term-Structure models'.

Official Electronic Trading Quantitative Analyst posting: 'perform thorough research on areas such as market microstructure and market impact analysis', 'design and spec new trading strategies with a particular focus on low latency trading strategies', 'analyze trading patterns and trends within market data (L2 or L3 format)', and 'employ modern data analytical tools such as machine learning but in a controlled and practical way'.

Same posting's skills list: 'working knowledge of Java (other languages considered)', 'proficient in data analysis using statistical software packages such as Python or equivalent', 'experience analyzing tick series market data via KDB / Onetick and extracting data via e.g. SQL', and 'knowledge of L3 market data and orderbook mechanics also a plus'.

UBS's official technology careers page states: 'UBS has more engineers and developers than many technology companies, and we're committed to a culture of engineering excellence', and that UBS aims 'to become an AI-enabled institution where all benefit from AI tooling'.

Inferred: graduate-programme structure and interview formats (online assessments, technical round counts) were not published on the retrieved pages; treat community reports as unconfirmed. Learners must consult https://www.ubs.com/global/en/careers.html and the official job board https://jobs.ubs.com/.

notes: UBS publishes concrete skill bars on its job board (jobs.ubs.com): the rates QA seat is explicitly Masters/PhD-level with C++/Python plus IR-derivatives calibration experience, while the electronic-trading QA seat is a Python/Java + SQL/KDB data-analysis role centred on microstructure, TCA and low-latency execution research, a in particular different skill mix under one 'quantitative analyst' title. Firmwide, UBS frames technology careers around engineering excellence, DevOps and becoming an AI-enabled institution. Not published: interview formats and assessment names, treat community reports as unverified. Note that www.ubs.com serves bot-protection to plain HTTP fetches; the pages cited here were retrieved via a real browser session.
